title_he: שִׂים בְּלִבִּי אַהֲבָה וַעֲשֵׂה מִמֶּנָּה נִגּוּן

lines: שִׂים בְּלִבִּי אַהֲבָה, עֲשֵׂה מִמֶּנָּה נִגּוּן
שִׂים בְּפִי דָּבָר וַעֲשֵׂה מִמֶּנּוּ שִׁירָה
שִׂים בְּשִׂכְלִי דַּעַת וַעֲשֵׂה מִמֶּנָּה אוֹר

review: The hymn is a prayer for the instruments of witness: 1:1–8 is Ps 40:4 with Col 3:16 and 2 Cor 3:18, 2:1–8 is Matt 9:36–38 with John 4:35 and John 14:6, and 3:1–8 is Matt 9:38 with 2 Tim 4:2 and Isa 6:8.

Stanza 1 repeats the same construction three times (שִׂים … וַעֲשֵׂה …), following the Arabic's ضَعْ … وَاصْنَعْ …; the Hebrew keeps the identical frame in all three, because the stanza's form is the threefold petition.

1:7–8 pair the light and the poured love as one clause, then name the ransom; the Hebrew keeps אַהֲבָתְךָ הַנִּשְׁפֶּכֶת (the poured-out love, per the glossary's נֶסֶךְ family) so that the line links to the cross rather than to a general affection.
